title: amygdalus spinosissima subsp. turcomanica
intro: Amygdalus spinosissima subsp. turcomanica, commonly known as Bukhara apricot kernel, is a plant species in the Prunus genus, native to Central Asia. It has been traditionally used for its health benefits, including reducing inflammation, alleviating pain, and exhibiting antimicrobial properties. The therapeutic actions of Bukhara apricot kernel include its ability to modulate the immune system, exhibit antioxidant activity, and show potential in treating various diseases. The bioactive constituents of Bukhara apricot kernel include amygdalin, a cyanogenic glycoside, as well as other compounds such as flavonoids and phenolic acids, which contribute to its medicinal properties.
